name: GUI-ReWalk: Massive Data Generation for GUI Agent via Stochastic Exploration and Intent-Aware Reasoning

name: Mind the Gap: Action Rebinding Attacks against Android GUI Agents

name: Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution

name: UI-Mem: Self-Evolving Experience Memory for Online Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Agents

name: MemGUI-Bench: Benchmarking Memory of Mobile GUI Agents in Dynamic Environments

name: MobileJailBench: Red Queen Jailbreak Benchmarking for Mobile Agents
notes: Reviewed the complete retained abstract and selected exact-v1 threat-model, construction and evaluation sections. Execution uses a browser-based Android-like simulator. The attacker controls instructions and designated carriers; privileged simulator state/APIs and system/model/harness internals remain outside attacker control. Rates depend on release, budget and adjudication coverage. SAF labels track observable expressions and actions; rate denominators exclude unresolved episodes.
summary: MobileJailBench evaluates mobile-agent jailbreaks in a browser-based Android-like simulator, combining feedback-driven attack evolution, separately admitted task expansions and evidence-grounded outcome adjudication.

name: MobileInject: Evaluating Reasoning-to-Action Security of MLLM-Based Mobile Agents under Cross-Modal Consistency Injection
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 construction, threat-model and evaluation sections. The attacker controls observation surfaces; system instructions, model parameters and the OS remain outside attacker control. State oracles are distinct from emitted-rationale diagnoses, whose labels include outcome-dependent constraints. Those diagnostics use outcome-dependent labels; hidden-reasoning causality remains unestablished.
summary: MobileInject evaluates visual/textual observation injection in stateful Android workflows using resettable emulators, benign/adversarial state oracles and trace-based diagnosis of emitted rationales and actions.

name: MacOS Agent (BIGAI)
notes: Released by the Computer-use-agents organization; the project page credits the BIGAI ML Group. macosagent/macosagent.py builds a smolagents CodeAgent whose tools are ten app agents (macosagent/agents/__init__.py): Browser, Calendar, Excel, Finder, Player, PowerPoint, Preview, TextEdit, WeChat and Word. The browser agent wraps the external browser-use library (agents/browser_agent/browser.py). In the Calendar agent, the window is captured with screencapture, interactive elements from the macOS accessibility API are drawn as numbered boxes on that screenshot, and the image plus element list go to the model (calendar/calendar.py, calendar/context.py, calendar/utils.py, agent/service.py); clicks and typing use pyautogui and pynput (controller/service.py). The Excel agent likewise clicks and types with pyautogui and runs AppleScript to save and close workbooks (excel_agent/controller/service.py). The README's License section names CC BY-NC 4.0, but the inspected tree has no license file.
summary: macOS agent in which a smolagents code agent dispatches per-application sub-agents that read accessibility trees and window screenshots and act through pyautogui mouse and keyboard input.

name: MemGUI-Bench
notes: Official benchmark code for the MemGUI-Bench paper (ACM MM 2026 per the README). The mg CLI pulls a prebuilt Docker runtime with the Android emulator and the MemGUI AVD snapshot, launches parallel backend containers on a Linux host with KVM, runs agents through MobileWorld's agent interface (src/mobile_world) and writes MobileWorld-format trajectories with screenshots. MemGUI-Eval (memgui_eval/) describes each step with a multimodal model and makes a final decision with a second model; the leaderboard uses Gemini 2.5 Flash and Gemini 2.5 Pro for these roles. Each task CSV row gives the app(s), difficulty, whether UI memory is required and golden steps; the default step budget is int(golden_steps * 2.5 + 1). The Hugging Face dataset lgy0404/MemGUI-Bench holds the same two task CSV files (byte-identical at revisions 217713e and 3fb01b6), so it is recorded as an alias.
summary: Memory-centric Android benchmark of 128 tasks across 26 apps, run in Dockerized emulators on a MobileWorld-style runtime and judged by MemGUI-Eval, an LLM evaluator reporting pass@k and memory metrics.

name: Uni-GUI-Desktop-1
notes: The UI-MOPD paper builds Uni-GUI from self-collected desktop and mobile trajectories plus cleaned OpenCUA and OpenMobile trajectories; its composition table rounds the self-collected desktop part to about 7K trajectories and 95K steps, so this repository (2,685 trajectories and about 36K steps per the card) holds a portion of it. Per the paper, desktop queries were generated with Kimi-K2.6 from functional points of initialized OSWorld environments, Kimi-K2.6 produced the rollouts and Gemini-3.1-Pro cleaned them; these are model-generated demonstrations. Every folder name ends in an OSWorld task ID: a script over the manifest finds 245 distinct IDs, all present in OSWorld's test_all.json, with up to 19 trajectories each. Two opened task.json files for the same OSWorld task label it 'OSWorld'; one repeats that task's instruction verbatim and the other paraphrases it, so the data overlaps OSWorld's test tasks. Both carry verified: false and task_completed: true, while the card's example shows verified: true; 160 folders also hold a result.txt. Linux is inferred from the paper's use of OSWorld environments and the Linux terminal and /home/user paths in the opened queries. Apache-2.0 is the card's declaration for the data. Only two task.json files and one result.txt were opened.
summary: Desktop trajectories from the UI-MOPD training data, collected in OSWorld environments: 2,685 tasks across 10 app categories with step screenshots, reasoning traces, normalized actions and pyautogui code.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: The code release scores each run for utility (required items shared) and contextual-integrity violation (prohibited items leaked), combining deterministic text matching against the scenario's must-share and must-not-share lists with an LLM judge at temperature 0; summaries report utility rate, leak rate and average reward.

A script recount of the released JSONL files matches every reported split and failure-mode count. The 50 test_e2e IDs all appear in test; seeds share separate IDs.

name: AgentCIBench
notes: Each scenario is a JSON snapshot of app states in the OpenApps workspace (messenger, todo, calendar, code editor, maps and shopping apps) with a task prompt and a disclosure policy. The card's test split serves the state-grounded reasoning track; test_e2e is a 50-scenario subset of it (all IDs overlap) for runs in the rendered UI, which the code README describes as a local multi-app web environment driven through Playwright; seeds holds 36 disjoint hand-written scenarios. The card says source is seed or mcts, but every released row reads seed or legacy_pilot_seed. The code repository linked as ukplab/arxiv2026-agentcibench now resolves to UKPLab/emnlp2026-agentcibench (GitHub API), and the card's second code link, agentcibench/agentcibench, returns 404. The 67.9% average leakage over 15 agents is a publisher figure. CC BY 4.0 is the card's data declaration; the code is a separate Apache-2.0 release.
summary: Contextual-integrity benchmark for computer-use agents: 117 synthetic multi-app workspace scenarios that pair under-specified requests with must-share and must-not-share lists, plus a 50-scenario live-UI subset.

name: Narada Code and OperatorMini
notes: The announcement says Narada Code tests workflows in a sandbox and can work with existing coding harnesses. Narada reports WebArena results for combined development and execution configurations.
summary: Narada Code develops and tests computer-use workflows, then revises them after failures. OperatorMini executes the instructions for repeatable web and enterprise tasks.
